_comment: Scions of the Divine names and terms. The English keys are the literal strings the game itself uses -- define sara = Character("Sarah") and the CHARACTER_DATA table in scripts/systems/definitions.rpy -- so a glossary entry can be checked against the source without guessing. tools/check.py enforces the `banned` lists against the 28 .rpy files this patch ships.
_banned_is_a_blunt_substring_match: banned is a plain substring search over the text the patch ships, with the canonical rendering removed first when the variant is a prefix of it. That makes 梅拉 a usable ban for Melany=梅拉妮 (the canonical is stripped, so it cannot fire on the correct spelling), but it also rules out several renderings that would otherwise be tempting. 神 is the most frequent character in this patch and appears in 神明 / 女神 / 神裔 / 神力 / 最后的真神, so no one-character term is pinned by ban -- they are pinned here by comment instead. 梅拉尼 is a prefix of nothing, but 拉 alone cannot be banned: it is the first character of 莱拉 and 阿斯塔拉 and the common noun 拉近, so those two names are pinned by comment. 原初 cannot be banned either -- it is the prefix of the canonical 原初者, and the checker only strips the canonical when the canonical is contained in the variant, not the other way round. Two entries had to be removed from the banned lists after check.py ran, because they are not variants at all: 凯特琳 is the correct rendering of Katelyn (the game has Kate introduce herself as "My name's Katelyn, but you can call me Kate.", so Kate and Katelyn are two spellings of one person and both have to exist), and 神灵 is the correct rendering of "the spirit of", which means soul or essence and is a different word from deity. Both are now their own entries. What is banned below are only renderings with no legitimate use: 萨拉 for 莎拉, 雷什盟 for 雷什蒙, and so on.
_doubling_exempt_note: Empty on purpose. The doubling rule looks for a canonical term immediately followed by its own last character -- 神裔裔, 守望者者, 莎拉拉 -- and none of this game's terms produce that shape anywhere in the 28 shipped scripts, so every term in this file is doubling-checked. The three that looked most likely to collide do not: 莱拉 + 拉 and 阿斯塔拉 + 拉 never end up adjacent in the Chinese (the verbs they would collide with are 拉近 / 拉远, and those lines do not put a 拉 immediately after the name), and 最后的真神 + 神 does not occur. Add a term here only together with a line of the patch that shows the collision.
_kept_verbatim_note: Fifteen strings the patch deliberately leaves in English. The first thirteen are names of the people, tools and platforms the credits page has to credit by their real names -- renaming someone's handle is not a translation decision. The last three are keyboard hints (Page Up / Page Down / Shift+A) and the profile sort key A-Z, which the game itself compares against as a machine value in screen_profiles_select.rpy. tools/check.py does not read this list for a script-override patch -- the equivalent guard for this layout is docs/glossary.json's banned lists, which do run -- but the list is recorded here because these are exactly the strings a later pass would otherwise 'fix' by mistake.

_developer_menu.note:
The developer menu is reachable by an ordinary player: screen_preferences.rpy has an image button that toggles persistent.dev_menu, which makes the 开发菜单 entry appear in the quick menu. It was translated in two passes -- the headings (开发菜单 / 章节选择 / 变量 / 档案 / 工具, and the 剧情开关 and 全部档案/全部服装/全部回忆 row labels) first, and the twelve action labels above afterwards, 36 occurrences in all. Nothing else in the patch is untranslated.
The English side of this screen is NOT all display text, and that is the trap: default dev_char_list = ["All"] and the comparisons dev_char_select == "All" are machine values, and "Outfits" / "Memories" / "Romanceable" / "Mages" are character tags. Only the first literal of a text/label/textbutton statement was replaced -- 36 sites, one pass, no other line touched. tools/verify_patch.cjs checks this screen by looking for the twelve English labels in display position only, so a machine value is never mistaken for an untranslated label.
